title: How AI is expanding what people do at work
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: OpenAI analyzes more than 800,000 U.S. ChatGPT work-related messages and finds substantial task crossover across occupations, reframing AI as a role-expansion tool rather than only a productivity layer.
actionable_takeaway: For every recurring automation, record which job roles it is borrowing from and update permissions, review gates and validation accordingly.

title: ChatGPT desktop app experience updates
author: OpenAI Help Center
why_it_matters: The desktop app now separates Chat, Work and Codex with a global switcher while unifying recents and project access, making entry-point boundaries more explicit.
actionable_takeaway: When launching a task, choose the mode by outcome: quick answer, deliverable work, or local repository execution; do not mix histories and permissions casually.

title: ChatGPT Work and Codex
author: OpenAI Help Center
why_it_matters: The help article clarifies Work, Codex, Voice, cloud sync, local chats and Remote access boundaries across web, mobile and desktop.
actionable_takeaway: Add an entry checklist covering execution environment, local-file access, history location, voice permissions and final review owner.

title: Work with Codex from anywhere
author: OpenAI
why_it_matters: Codex Remote turns mobile into a live control plane for connected hosts, approvals, diffs, terminal output and project context without moving credentials to the phone.
actionable_takeaway: Use iPhone for steering, questions and low-risk approvals; keep diff-heavy review, commits, pushes and deploys on the Mac host.

title: Enterprise managed settings in the GitHub Copilot app and Copilot cloud agent
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub Copilot app and cloud agent now obey enterprise managed settings for plugin and marketplace controls, closing governance gaps across agent surfaces.
actionable_takeaway: Centralize plugin, network, approval-bypass and model defaults in one policy instead of configuring every client separately.

title: Manage GitHub Copilot app access with a dedicated policy
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub split Copilot app access from the Copilot CLI policy, recognizing that different clients need separately managed access decisions.
actionable_takeaway: Create an entry-permission matrix for mobile, desktop, CLI, cloud and local agents instead of assuming one authorization covers all entry points.

title: GitHub Mobile: Fix failing Actions checks with Copilot cloud agent
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub Mobile can trigger Copilot cloud agent from a failed Actions check; the agent opens a follow-up PR and requests review before merge.
actionable_takeaway: Treat phone-triggered fixes as draft work: investigate, patch and notify, then return to desktop for review, tests and merge decisions.

title: Copilot cloud agent for Linear is now generally available
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Linear issues can be assigned to Copilot cloud agent, which analyzes the issue, works in an ephemeral environment, streams updates and opens a draft PR for review.
actionable_takeaway: When using issue-driven agents, require base branch, working branch, model, custom agent guidance and review ownership per issue.

title: Agent automation controls in GitHub Issues in public preview
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub Issues now supports rationale, confidence and approval review for agent changes to labels, fields, issue type, closing and assignments.
actionable_takeaway: Use rationale and confidence as standard metadata for AI Radar signal classification and hold low-confidence actions for user review.

title: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: GitHub MCP Server supports the July 28, 2026 stateless MCP spec and points to conformance tests for validating clients and servers.
actionable_takeaway: For local or private MCP tools, verify stateless behavior, auth, logging, secret scanning and elicitation rather than only checking connectivity.

title: Copilot code review: Customization and configurability improvements
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: Copilot code review now reads custom instructions from the head branch, supports dedicated setup steps, firewall defaults and separate runner settings.
actionable_takeaway: Review agents need their own setup, network and instruction validation path, separate from general coding agents.

title: Security reviews now available in the GitHub Copilot app
author: GitHub Changelog
why_it_matters: The Copilot app adds a /security-review command for high-confidence findings, severity/confidence scoring and actionable fixes before code lands.
actionable_takeaway: Add on-demand security review before public deploys or automation changes that touch auth, paths, secrets, external fetches or generated assets.

title: Agentic coding and persistent returns to expertise
author: Anthropic Research
why_it_matters: Anthropic's analysis of about 400,000 Claude Code sessions finds people make most planning decisions while the agent makes most execution decisions; domain expertise increases agent productivity.
actionable_takeaway: Prompt agents with outcome, constraints, domain context and verification evidence, then let them choose implementation steps within the boundary.

title: Agent view in Claude Code
author: Anthropic
why_it_matters: Claude Code's agent view centralizes running, waiting and completed sessions, reinforcing the need for a status dashboard when multiple coding agents run in parallel.
actionable_takeaway: Track Codex threads by status, blocker, artifact, validation and owner instead of scattering long-running work across terminals.

title: Creator of Anthropic's Claude Code wants you to stop micromanaging your AI
author: Business Insider
why_it_matters: The article reports advice from Claude Code creator Boris Cherny: state the desired outcome and boundaries instead of over-specifying every step for modern coding agents.
actionable_takeaway: Replace step-by-step micromanagement prompts with result, constraints, forbidden actions, evidence and stop conditions.
